clue.text: Approach about money and shelter that's effective

indicators.note: here 'about' means surrounding: the approach word goes round the money letter

parts.note: to approach is to come
P stands for pence, British small money
a tent is a simple shelter

explanation.surface: Someone praises a housing scheme combining cash and refuge as effective.
explanation.definitionFit: Something capable and adequate for its job is effective.

clue.text: Love to write music out-of-doors

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O
to pen is to write
an air is a tune, a piece of music

explanation.surface: A romantic likes to compose songs outside.
explanation.definitionFit: An outdoor event takes place in the fresh air, outside buildings.

clue.text: The price of wrong-doing is coppers holding one

indicators.note: the coins word holds the word for one inside it, so it is a container

parts.note: coppers are copper coins, British pence
an is the indefinite article, meaning one

explanation.surface: A remark that small coins hold the cost of sinning, or that police are holding a suspect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coppers' suggests police; here it means small coins.
explanation.definitionFit: An act of atonement is the cost a sinner pays for doing wrong.

clue.text: A sober individual imbibing each and every drink? A likely story!

indicators.note: imbibing means drinking in, so the sober person takes the next word inside

parts.note: TT is a teetotaller, one who never drinks alcohol
all means each and every one
ale is a drink, beer

explanation.surface: A teetotaller claims to be swallowing every drink going, which nobody believes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A likely story!' is said sarcastically of something implausible.
explanation.definitionFit: An exaggerated, unbelievable yarn is greeted sarcastically with that phrase.

clue.text: Coin once used as a special gift

definitions.meaning: a weight and unit of money in the ancient world, such as in biblical parables
a natural aptitude or flair someone possesses

explanation.definitionFit: The biblical money unit gave English its word for a God-given ability, through the parable of the servants.

clue.text: In the tall grass mildew formed, not for the first time

definitions.text: formed, not for the first time

indicators.note: 'In' puts the mildew word inside the grass word, a container

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass growing by water
mildew is a mould, a fungal growth

explanation.surface: Mildew develops repeatedly in long grass.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaped again, as with a retreaded tyre, means made a second time.

clue.text: A couple in accommodation fit only for animals-it's really too much!

indicators.note: 'in' places the pair of pieces inside the animal housing word

parts.note: a sty is a pen for pigs
to couple is to tie together

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a pair being housed like livestock is beyond the pale.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a cryptic paraphrase: the state of having had more than enough.
explanation.definitionFit: Being glutted, having had more than enough, is exactly a feeling of excess.

clue.text: Going back, reorganised services without point

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so the compass point stands beyond the rearranged letters
reorganised says the letters of the given word are rearranged

parts.note: E is east, a compass point

explanation.surface: Services, restructured without any purpose, are in retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but means 'outside': RECESSIV, the anagram of SERVICES, is followed by E.
explanation.definitionFit: Receding, as a hairline does, is moving backwards.

clue.text: To state the time is quite usual

parts.note: to aver is to state firmly
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Telling the time is nothing out of the ordinary.
explanation.definitionFit: Typical or normal, the middle of the range, is the ordinary standard.

clue.text: Sound military leaders can appear nuts!

indicators.note: Sound tells us the word is as spoken, so a soundalike spelling goes in

parts.note: colonels are senior army officers

explanation.surface: Healthy army commanders may seem crazy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like 'healthy'; 'nuts' looks like 'mad' but means edible seeds.
explanation.definitionFit: The edible inner parts of nuts are seeds; the plural here names those nut centres.

clue.text: Oriental spur occasioning strong feeling

parts.note: E is East, the Orient
a motive spurs someone to act

explanation.surface: An Eastern incentive stirs deep passions.
explanation.definitionFit: Arousing intense passion describes stirring language.

clue.text: Curse and stop the race

parts.note: to dam is to stop a flow
a nation is a people or race

explanation.surface: Someone swears and halts a running contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'race' suggests a contest but means a people.
explanation.definitionFit: Damnation is used as an oath, an exclamation of swearing.

clue.text: Sporting persons who don't look ahead

definitions.text: Sporting persons who don't look ahead

parts.words: Sporting persons who don't look ahead
parts.note: rowers sit facing the stern, so they move forward while looking backwards

explanation.definitionFit: Rowers face backwards to propel the boat forwards.

clue.text: The least well prepared sportsmen

indicators.note: well prepared suggests the letters are made ready in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A paradox: the least ready competitors.
explanation.definitionFit: Track and field competitors are sportsmen.

clue.text: Test an alternative to wood

parts.note: or introduces an alternative
deal is pine or fir timber

explanation.surface: A trial offering a choice in place of timber.
explanation.definitionFit: A trial or severe test of endurance.

clue.text: The crooked prosper, so a despot found

indicators.note: crooked means bent out of shape, so the letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: The dishonest thrive, and so a tyrant is established.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crooked' reads as describing villains but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A tyrant is one who rules harshly and keeps people down.

clue.text: Dope records are necessary, they agree

parts.note: a dope is a fool, an ass
to enter is to record, as in a ledger

explanation.surface: Drug test results are required, and the authorities consent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dope' suggests drugs but means a fool; 'records' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who say yes to a proposal are people who consent.

clue.text: By the shore setting seed is a problem

indicators.note: setting means arranging, so these letters are placed in a new order

explanation.surface: Planting seeds on the coast proves difficult.
explanation.definitionFit: The coast, by the sea, is the holiday shore area.

clue.text: Free from engagements, many cut down on food

indicators.note: in a down clue 'on' means placed after the food word

parts.note: a date is a fruit
less is a reduced amount, many cut down

explanation.surface: Lots of people are reducing their eating, and are free of commitments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engagements' suggests betrothals, but means appointments such as dates.
explanation.definitionFit: Having no appointments, without a social date in the diary.

clue.text: Clemency, but not for all

definitions.meaning: mercy shown to a beaten enemy, as in giving no such thing
a fraction, a fourth part, not the whole

explanation.definitionFit: Mercy to the vanquished, and one fourth, a part rather than the whole.

clue.text: Stick a little notice in this spot

parts.note: an ad is a short advertisement, a notice
here means in this place

explanation.surface: Put up a small poster right here.
explanation.definitionFit: To cling or be glued to something is to stick.

clue.text: The woman going around with trainee manager

indicators.note: the woman's word encloses the next pieces

parts.note: her refers to a woman
and means with, together
L is a learner driver, a trainee

explanation.surface: A woman goes about with a trainee boss.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who manages a boxer or animal, controlling them.

clue.text: A composer in a maestro's sinister clutches

indicators.note: clutches means the words hold the answer within them

explanation.surface: A composer caught in a conductor's evil grip.
explanation.walkthrough: Gioachino Rossini, Italian opera composer of The Barber of Seville.
explanation.definitionFit: Rossini was an Italian opera composer.

clue.text: A game played as permitted in the road

indicators.note: in places the permitted word inside the road word

parts.note: a route is a road
let means allowed

explanation.surface: A game allowed to be played in the street.
explanation.definitionFit: A casino wheel game of chance.

clue.text: Tea's in fashion as a beverage

indicators.note: to fashion is to shape, so these letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: Tea is trendy as a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tea's' is 'tea is', so the S counts.
explanation.definitionFit: A herbal infusion is a drink.

clue.text: Place made popular by a writer with some craft

parts.note: in means fashionable, popular
Jules Verne, French science-fiction writer
SS is a steamship, a craft

explanation.surface: A town made famous by an author and his boat.
explanation.walkthrough: INVERNESS is a city in the Scottish Highlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Inverness is a city in Scotland.

clue.text: Priests can be impish creatures!

indicators.note: can be signals that the letters can be rearranged into another word

explanation.surface: Clergy can be mischievous.
explanation.definitionFit: Elves and fairies are mischievous spirits.

clue.text: Having about a hundred pounds, mean to save

parts.note: re means about, concerning
C is the Roman numeral 100
L stands for libra, pounds
to mean is to aim, to intend

explanation.surface: Someone with roughly £100 intends to put money aside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'save' means rescue or recover, not keep money.
explanation.definitionFit: To recover or retrieve, as in saving waste.

clue.text: Go on too long about backing railway workers

parts.note: over means about, concerning

indicators.note: backing means the union's letters are read in reverse

parts.note: NUR, the British National Union of Railwaymen

explanation.surface: A meeting supporting rail staff overruns its time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' looks like support but reverses NUR.
explanation.definitionFit: To exceed a time limit is to go beyond it.

clue.text: Looks over suite-makes complaint

parts.note: eyes means looks at
a train is a retinue, suite

explanation.surface: Someone inspects a furniture set and grumbles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suite' suggests furniture but means an entourage.
explanation.definitionFit: A tired, sore condition of vision is an ailment.
